business_problem: Formula E wanted fan experiences that feel immediate, immersive, personalized, and participatory, but its broadcast and event experience was limited by inconsistent onboard video quality, information spread across multiple sources, and race data that viewers could not easily follow through the live broadcast alone.
solution_summary: Formula E worked with Lenovo on three AI-enabled fan-experience implementations spanning broadcast quality, conversational discovery, and augmented race storytelling. For AI Video Optimization, actual onboard footage from Jeddah night racing and Monaco daytime racing is ingested from in-car cameras and processed by AI that dynamically corrects glare, haze, exposure, and color shifts, enabling near-real-time enhancement for live broadcast workflows. For the AI Fan Experience Guide, Formula E content about drivers, cars, circuits, rules, history, and venue guidance is prepared, structured, and grounded in a connected knowledge base; Lenovo xIQ performs retrieval and response generation behind a lifelike digital human that serves fast answers to fan questions. For AR broadcast graphics, Formula E live vehicle and race data is processed and integrated into an in-car heads-up display that overlays telemetry such as speed, energy, ATTACK MODE, laps, G-force, position, gaps, and trajectory without obstructing sponsor content.

solution_components.name: AI Video Optimization
solution_components.role: Processes onboard race footage to correct glare, haze, exposure, and color inconsistencies for near-real-time broadcast enhancement.

solution_components.name: AI Fan Experience Guide
solution_components.role: Provides a conversational digital-human interface that lets fans ask about Formula E knowledge and venue guidance.

solution_components.name: Lenovo xIQ
solution_components.role: Handles Formula E knowledge retrieval and response generation behind the digital-human fan experience.

solution_components.name: AR broadcast graphics
solution_components.role: Adds live race and vehicle telemetry into the in-car broadcast view as readable augmented overlays.

data_flow: Onboard camera feeds from Formula E races are sent to AI Video Optimization for near-real-time image correction before broadcast use. Formula E content from multiple sources is prepared and structured into a connected knowledge base, then Lenovo xIQ retrieves and grounds answers for the digital-human interface. Separately, live vehicle and race data flows from Formula E broadcast workflows into Lenovo processing and HUD integration, then appears as AR overlays in the in-car broadcast view.
integration_points: Onboard car camera footage from Formula E races
Formula E content sources covering drivers, cars, circuits, rules, history, and venue guidance
Live vehicle and race data from Formula E broadcast workflows
business_outcome: Formula E validated near-real-time AI video enhancement, launched a fan guide with high answer accuracy and sub-second responses, and created an AR broadcast concept that can strengthen fan engagement, reduce routine support pressure, improve broadcast value, and open new sponsorship and revenue opportunities.
metrics: The system completed image enhancement in under three seconds.
The AI brought the color balance of green-tinted night footage to 3.4x its original level.
More than 95% answer accuracy across the connected knowledge base.
Delivered responses in under one second.
More than 10 real-time data points directly within the in-car broadcast view.
Less than one second between live vehicle data and the information appearing on screen.
architecture_clues: Video-enhancement pilot used actual onboard footage from night racing in Jeddah and daytime racing in Monaco.
Image enhancement was tested and validated by Formula E for near-real-time broadcast correction.
The fan-guide system used a connected knowledge base with grounded retrieval and response generation behind a lifelike digital human.
AR HUD design was centered on a selected car and key race moment while avoiding obstruction of sponsor content.
The approach was designed to extend across different circuits, weather conditions, racing environments, races, and venues.
